recent_posts.title: Securing the Supply Chain, One API Call at a Time: Inside the SecurityScorecard API Hackathon
recent_posts.summary: SecurityScorecard hosted its first API Hackathon, bringing together global developers and cybersecurity professionals to build automation tools for supply chain risk management. Over 50% of participants were new to APIs, yet they created practical solutions including vulnerability tracking tools, risk visualization dashboards, and vendor assessment integrations with popular platforms like Google Sheets and Slack. The event highlighted strong demand for beginner-friendly API documentation and real-world templates, with participants primarily focused on automation goals.

recent_posts.title: Scorecarder Spotlight: Guillermo Garcia Granda
recent_posts.summary: Guillermo Garcia Granda, a Field Sales Account Director for LATAM at SecurityScorecard, shares his journey pursuing a Master's degree in Governance, Risk, and Compliance. With over 20 years in cybersecurity, he explains how the program helps him bridge technical expertise with strategic business understanding, enabling him to better serve clients as a trusted advisor who can communicate effectively with both technical teams and boardroom executives across Latin America.

recent_posts.title: How STRIKE Helped Identify Qakbot’s Alleged Operator and Support a $24M Asset Seizure
recent_posts.summary: The SecurityScorecard STRIKE team aided U.S. law enforcement in a long-term investigation of Qakbot, a malware used by ransomware groups. Russian national Rustam Rafailevich Gallyamov was indicted, leading to $24 million in seized assets. The disruption marked a shift from infrastructure takedown to actor attribution. Gallyamov operated Qakbot since 2008, supporting major ransomware activities, and faces up to 25 years in prison if convicted.

recent_posts.title: What Are 10 Major Industry-Specific Cybersecurity Regulations?
recent_posts.summary: Cybersecurity regulations in 2025 are increasingly tailored to specific industries, addressing sector-specific threats and data sensitivities. For healthcare, finance, retail, and other sectors, compliance frameworks like HIPAA, GLBA, PCI DSS, and CMMC are critical. Organizations must adopt continuous monitoring, real-time visibility, and robust data protection measures to ensure compliance and resilience. SecurityScorecard offers tools and services to assist businesses in maintaining cybersecurity readiness amidst evolving regulations.

recent_posts.title: 10 Best Practices for Securing Protected Health Information (PHI): What Is PHI and How To Secure It
recent_posts.summary: Protected Health Information (PHI) comprises any identifiable health-related data used within medical care, governed by HIPAA regulations. Due to its long-term value, PHI is frequently targeted by cybercriminals for identity theft and fraud. Securing PHI involves practices such as classification, encryption, access controls, user monitoring, and staff training. Healthcare organizations must also ensure compliance through third-party agreements and develop robust incident response plans to manage breaches effectively.

recent_posts.title: SecurityScorecard Advisory: Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite XSS Vulnerability (CVE-2024-27443) Added to CISA KEV
recent_posts.summary: The Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite has a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability (CVE-2024-27443) that has been added to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (CISA KEV) catalog. This highlights the critical importance of addressing security weaknesses in collaborative software platforms.

recent_posts.title: What Is an Exploit? Understanding Vulnerabilities and Threat Mitigation
recent_posts.summary: Exploits are methods used to leverage software vulnerabilities for unauthorized access or disruption. Key exploit types like remote code execution, SQL injection, and zero-day exploits highlight varied attack methods. Effective defense requires understanding exploit lifecycles, using vulnerability management, and deploying secure development practices to mitigate threats.

recent_posts.title: LDAP vs. Active Directory: Understanding the Differences
recent_posts.summary: LDAP is a protocol used to access directory services, widely utilized for interoperability with non-Windows systems, while Active Directory is a Microsoft proprietary directory service offering centralized user authentication and device management within Windows networks. Both have security implications and require proper configuration to reduce risks such as credential theft and unauthorized access.

recent_posts.title: What Is Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) and How Is It Used in Cybersecurity?
recent_posts.summary: Open source intelligence (OSINT) involves collecting publicly available data for cybersecurity purposes, aiding in threat detection and incident response. Both attackers and defenders use OSINT for various purposes, including identifying vulnerabilities and monitoring third-party risks. Legal and ethical use of OSINT ensures credibility in cybersecurity operations, with tools like Shodan, Maltego, and Google Dorking playing crucial roles. Best practices include automating data collection and correlating findings with security logs.

recent_posts.title: How Do You Identify and Prevent Phishing Attacks in 2025?
recent_posts.summary: Phishing attacks continue to be a major threat in 2025, with sophisticated tactics powered by artificial intelligence, such as hyper-targeted emails and deepfakes. Effective prevention requires real-time detection, proactive education, and intelligent visibility into third-party risks. Recognize psychological triggers in phishing attempts, embrace multi-layered security methods, and utilize AI-enhanced tools to safeguard against these evolving threats.
